title: Patient-specific compounding and significant difference
rule_summary: Massachusetts defines compounding to include patient-specific preparation and permits use of a commercially available product as a component when the compounded preparation produces, for that patient, a significant difference determined by the prescriber. A difference in price alone does not constitute the required significant difference.
exam_relevance: Tests a practical non-hazardous compounding boundary without relying on hazardous or sterile engineering-control details.
common_confusions: Lower price by itself is not the patient-specific significant difference contemplated by the statute.
verification_notes: Current official Massachusetts authority verified during Pre-Batch3 T2 authoring on 2026-08-18; fresh independent legal and realism audit is still required before release.
